title: Equal sides do not prove square
hook: Which shape has equal diagonals in this example?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: A parallelogram can retain opposite side lengths while its corners skew. Its two diagonals differ unless the included angle is ninety degrees in this example; a diagonal comparison detects the skew.

misconception: The two pictured methods are interchangeable without checking their mechanism or constraints.

recall.question: A frame has equal opposite sides, 60 cm and 80 cm. Its diagonals measure about 104 cm and 96 cm. What does that tell you?
recall.why: Equal opposite sides make a parallelogram, which can still skew. Its diagonals are equal only when the corners are 90°; these differ, so the frame is out of square.
